My top five are **c043, c049, c037, c036, and c015**.

I parsed the POSCAR structures and compared their symmetry, coordination environments, composition, and structural prototypes with the training set. I also checked descriptor-based regression models. Importantly, a large strain coefficient requires both a piezoelectric response and substantial elastic compliance: \(d=e\,C^{-1}\). Noncentrosymmetry alone is not enough.

| Rank | Candidate | Structural reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **c043 — K3SbS4** | Its **\(I\bar{4}3m\)** structure closely matches both **Na3SbS4 (149.3 pC/N)** and **TaTl3S4 (132.5 pC/N)**. This is the strongest high-response prototype match in the pool. The expanded potassium-containing lattice also favors compliance. |
| **2** | **c049 — ZnCl2** | This particular polymorph has the **\(I\bar{4}2d\)** tetrahedral framework found in **GeS2 (38.3)**, **GeSe2 (38.5)**, and **TiS2 (104.5 pC/N)**. Its relatively soft Zn–Cl framework makes it a strong candidate for enhanced shear strain response. |
| **3** | **c037 — Tl3SbS3** | Its polar **\(R3m\)** structure closely resembles **Tl3AsS3 (35.7)** and **Tl3AsSe3 (36.5 pC/N)**. The heavy, polarizable ions and asymmetric coordination support a substantial response. |
| **4** | **c036 — SiS2** | Another close **\(I\bar{4}2d\)** framework match to the high-response dichalcogenides. Stronger Si–S bonding may reduce compliance relative to the germanium analogues, but the structural evidence remains favorable. |
| **5** | **c015 — CuI** | The **zincblende \(F\bar{4}3m\)** polymorph allows shear piezoelectricity and has a soft, polarizable Cu–I tetrahedral network. It ranked consistently well in the descriptor models, although its high-response training analogies are less direct than those above. |

**c043 is my clearest first choice.** The ordering of the remaining four is less certain, particularly because unusually soft elastic modes cannot be determined reliably from equilibrium structures alone.

Final: c043, c049, c037, c036, c015
